The National Sports Commission has rewarded Nigeria’s three Youth Olympic gold medallists with $20,000 each, following their historic performance at the Games in Dakar, Senegal. The beneficiaries are Bright Gift, who won the men’s 100m in a Games record of 10.28 seconds, Rosemary Chigozie Nwankwo, who won the women’s 100m in 11.16 seconds, and Praise Tejiri Ugoh, who won the women’s 400m in a personal best of 52.76 seconds. The NSC announced the reward in a statement signed by the Special Assistant on Media to the Director General, Kola Daniel, on Wednesday. It follows the N100m reward given by President Bola Tinubu to the Flamingos, and the NSC said the athletes had not been left out of the celebrations. The Commission described the gesture as part of its commitment to reward excellence, motivate young athletes and ensure that no category of Nigerian champions is left behind in the ongoing sports reforms. They added that the reward reflects the recognition of their dedication and patriotism on the global stage, and aligns with the Renewed Hope Agenda for sports, which prioritises athlete welfare, grassroots development, early discovery of talent and a sustainable reward system for podium performances. Youth Olympics: NOC awards $1,000 to gold medallists Dakar 2026: Nigeria’s best-ever Youth Olympics outing Scrabble champions deserve more support – Coach Ikola The NSC said more structured incentive packages were being put in place for athletes who win medals at continental and global competitions, including the African Games, the Commonwealth Games, the World Championships and the Olympic Games. The three golds were Nigeria’s best-ever outing at the Youth Olympics, surpassing the previous best of two at the inaugural edition in Singapore in 2010. The Commission praised the athletes for their resilience, focus and conduct, and urged them to remain disciplined and serve as role models to millions of young Nigerians. They also thanked President Tinubu for his support for sports development, describing his leadership as a turning point for the sector.
